newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel and Palestinians reach accord on debts.
newsitem.headline: Israel and Palestinians reach accord on debts.

text.p: Israel and the Palestinian Authority (PA) have agreed on a mechanism for settling mutual debts, Israel's Treasury said on Wednesday.

"We can report that after conducting negotiations that went well between the Treasury and the Palestinian Authority that we have reached an agreement that will eliminate all the past debts the Palestinians claimed they are owed by Israel," said Israeli Finance Minister Dan Meridor in a statement.
"In addition we have agreed on a mechanism under which all the (Israeli) institutions owed money by the PA will get their money in the future," he said.
The agreement came at a meeting between Meridor and Nabil Shaath, Palestininan minister for economic cooperation. The two agreed to meet again in two weeks.

Israel owes the PA 105 million shekels ($30 million), of which 65 million shekels is from value added tax from May to December 1994. Under the agreement Israel will pay the money owed within the next two weeks.

The Treasury said the PA owed Israeli organisations, mainly hospitals, the Mekorot water company and Bezeq Israel Telcom, a total of 75 million shekels. But Israel had already deducted the amount from the tax receipts due Palestinians, the Treasury said.
